title: Mesh quarantine and fractional traffic-bleed for live session continuity
creator: Amrita Shah
description:
Problem: In active-active hosted API deployments, abrupt region isolation (network flaps, infra incidents) causes large-volume traffic shifts that break long-lived streaming sessions and amplify load on healthy regions. Existing failover strategies bluntly drain or redirect traffic which yields stale KV caches, truncated streams, and amplification of cold-start loads.

Goal: Implement a mesh-level quarantine + fractional traffic-bleed mechanism that: (1) isolates suspected-degraded edge regions without instantly severing user streams, (2) progressively migrates new and in-flight requests with session-aware routing, and (3) leverages circuit-breaker signals and SLO headroom to bound failover-induced tail-latency and cost. The mechanism should be observable, allow manual overrides, and integrate with rollout policies and autoscaling signals.

Scope: design and implementation of traffic-steering algorithms at the regional gateway mesh, session-safe fractional bleed window for short-lived and long-lived streams, circuit-breaker thresholds for mesh quarantine, KV-prefetch / cache-warm strategies for migrated sessions, and Console dashboards for SLO drift and traffic-bleed metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Can quarantine a region so it receives zero new steady-state egress but continues to serve active in-flight streams for up to configurable grace period
New connections are probabilistically routed away from quarantined regions based on a configurable bleed rate (0-100%) and SLO headroom
Streaming clients continue without abrupt connection termination when possible (handoff or transparent proxied relay) for at least the configured grace period
Circuit-breaker trips at mesh-edge when 95th-percentile latency or error-rate cross thresholds and automatically reduces bleed rate or engages full quarantine
KV cache warm-up for migrated sessions reduces cold-start token cost by at least 40% in benchmarked tests
Console surfaces per-region bleed-rate, quarantined state, migrated-session counts, and estimated cost delta
E2E test harness simulates region flaps and validates no more than 2x temporary error spike and recovery within configured SLO window
implementation_notes: Traffic steering will be implemented as a middleware on the gateway mesh that supports fractional traffic diversion via consistent hashing + reinforced session affinity metadata
Fractional bleed uses a token-bucket probability sampler keyed on session-id for sticky decisioning of long-lived streams

Mesh quarantine toggles will be written as two-stage states: 'observe' (metrics-only), 'soft-quarantine' (fractional bleed + reduced new-conn handshake acceptance), and 'hard-quarantine' (no new conns)
Circuit-breaker parameters: sliding window 60s, min 500 requests, error-rate threshold 3%, p95 latency threshold configurable per-model/route
KV cache sync: on migration, gateway will asynchronously prefetch top-N KV keys using a prioritized warm-up queue; fallback uses on-demand streaming of missing keys
Autoscaler integration: when bleed increases healthy-region load beyond autoscale thresholds, trigger accelerated scale-up and temporarily lower bleed rate until capacity stabilizes
Rollback: provide immediate manual revert to 'observe' state and an automated backoff policy if downstream SLOs deteriorate
risks: Too-aggressive bleed may overload healthy regions and trigger cascading failures
Complexity in migrating in-flight KV-dependent streams could cause correctness regressions for stateful sessions
Significant operational overhead if quarantine flaps due to noisy metrics; requires robust debounce logic
Cost regression if warm-up or duplication of requests is not bounded
Client compatibility: some third-party SDKs may not support transparent stream handoff and will require explicit client-side reconnect guidance
milestones: Integration with circuit-breaker + KV warm-up path — 2025-03-10
Canary on staging with SLO guardrails — 2025-03-17
Gradual rollout to region US-West-2 (dedicated canary) — 2025-03-24
comments: 2025-02-13: Kickoff sync — decided to favor probabilistic session steering over synchronous handoff for initial phase to limit cross-region state transfer.
2025-02-18: Design review — PM requested explicit console flags for operator-initiated 'circuit quarantine' and audit trail. Action: add audit events for each state transition (ENG-98123-AT).
2025-02-22: Performance note from infra — prefetching too many KV keys during migration spikes GPU memory for small instances. Action: implement rate-limited warm-up queue and LRU cap per instance.
2025-02-25: Security review requested — cross-region key use for KV prefetch needs KMS policy review. Security owner: Priya Raman. Ticket created: SEC-4783.
2025-02-27: QA findings — simulated 30% bleed caused 1.8x transient error rate in small-region canary; mitigations proposed (lower initial bleed, faster autoscale).
2025-03-01: PM feedback — include customer-facing guidance for SDKs: best-effort reconnection semantics and recommended retry/backoff. Added to docs epic (PM-1102).
